name: Auto Capitalize Names by AyudaWP
author: Fernando Tellado

sections.description:
Auto Capitalize Names by AyudaWP ensures all customer names in your WordPress and WooCommerce site are properly capitalized, maintaining professional consistency across your entire platform.

The Problem It Solves

Many website owners face issues with inconsistent name formatting:

  • Customers entering names in all lowercase during registration or checkout
  • Unprofessional-looking reports and invoices with incorrect capitalization
  • Billing errors and disputes due to mismatched name formats
  • Poor data quality affecting marketing efforts and customer communications
  • Manual correction of thousands of existing records

This plugin was born from a real client need: ensuring invoice reports had correctly formatted names to avoid billing discrepancies and maintain professional standards.

Key Features

  • Automatic Capitalization: Capitalizes names in real-time during:

    • WordPress user registration and profile updates
    • WooCommerce checkout process
    • Admin edits of users, customers, and orders
    • My Account address updates

  • Smart Name Handling:

    • Compound names with hyphens (María-José → María-José)
    • Multilingual particles kept lowercase (de, la, van, von, da, etc.)
    • Multiple word names (Ana María del Carmen)
    • UTF-8 support for international characters

  • Multilingual Support: Includes default particles for:

    • Spanish: de, la, del, las, los, y
    • French: du, des, le
    • Italian: di, da, degli, dei, della
    • Dutch: van, van de, van der, de, den
    • German: von, vom, von der, zu, zur
    • Portuguese: da, do, das, dos

  • Customizable Particles: Add your own lowercase particles for other languages or regional variants

  • Bulk Database Tool:

    • Preview changes before applying
    • Selectively capitalize user names, addresses, or orders
    • Safe operation with detailed change preview
    • One-time fix for existing database records
    • Detailed breakdown of changes made

  • HPOS Compatible: Full support for WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage

What Gets Capitalized

WordPress Users:
– First name (first_name)
– Last name (last_name)

WooCommerce Customers:
– Billing first and last names
– Shipping first and last names

WooCommerce Orders:
– Billing first and last names
– Shipping first and last names

Benefits

  • Professional Appearance: Consistent formatting across all documents and reports
  • Invoice Accuracy: Reduce billing errors and customer disputes
  • Better Data Quality: Clean database for analytics and marketing
  • Legal Compliance: Proper names on official documents and receipts
  • Time Saving: No manual correction needed
  • User Experience: Customers see their names formatted correctly
  • International Ready: Works with names from multiple languages and cultures

How to Use

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Names will automatically capitalize from now on
  3. (Optional) Go to Users > Capitalize Names > Plugin Settings
  4. (Optional) Add custom particles for your specific needs
  5. Go to Users > Capitalize Names to fix existing records
  6. Select what to capitalize (users, addresses, orders)
  7. Check the required backup confirmation
  8. Preview changes before executing
  9. Execute to apply changes to your database

Name Examples

The plugin correctly handles:
– Simple names: “john smith” → “John Smith”
– Accented names: “josé garcía” → “José García”
– Hyphenated names: “maría-josé” → “María-José”
– Spanish particles: “juan de la cruz” → “Juan de la Cruz”
– Dutch names: “vincent van gogh” → “Vincent van Gogh”
– German names: “ludwig von beethoven” → “Ludwig von Beethoven”
– French names: “charles de gaulle” → “Charles de Gaulle”
– Portuguese names: “vasco da gama” → “Vasco da Gama”
sections.installation:
Automatic Installation

  1. Log in to your WordPress admin panel
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New
  3. Search for “Auto Capitalize Names by AyudaWP”
  4. Click Install Now and then Activate

Manual Installation

  1. Download the plugin zip file
  2. Log in to your WordPress admin panel
  3. Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin
  4. Choose the zip file and click Install Now
  5. Activate the plugin

After Installation

  1. Go to Users > Capitalize Names
  2. Read the information about what the plugin does
  3. (Optional) Add custom particles in Plugin Settings
  4. Use the bulk tool to capitalize existing names (optional)
  5. Test by creating a new user with lowercase names
sections.faq:
Does this work with existing names in my database?

Yes! The plugin includes a bulk tool to capitalize all existing names. Go to Users > Capitalize Names and use the preview feature to see what will change before applying.

Will it work with names in other languages?

Yes, the plugin uses UTF-8 encoding and properly handles international characters including accents, tildes, and special characters. It includes default particles for Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, German, and Portuguese.

Can I add support for other languages?

Yes! Go to Users > Capitalize Names > Plugin Settings and add custom particles separated by commas. For example, if you need support for Scottish names, you could add “mac, mc” to the custom particles field.

What about compound names with hyphens?

The plugin correctly handles hyphenated names like “María-José” or “Jean-Claude”, capitalizing each part independently.

Does it handle naming conventions from different cultures?

Yes! The plugin respects particles (de, la, van, von, da, etc.) keeping them in lowercase. For example: “Juan de la Cruz” not “Juan De La Cruz”, or “Vincent van Gogh” not “Vincent Van Gogh”.

Is it compatible with WooCommerce HPOS?

Yes, the plugin fully supports High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and works seamlessly with both HPOS and legacy storage systems.

Will it slow down my site?

No. The plugin only processes names when they’re being saved, causing no performance impact during normal site operation.

Can I undo the bulk changes?

The bulk changes are permanent, which is why the plugin shows a detailed preview before executing and requires you to confirm you’ve made a database backup.

Does it work with custom registration forms?

It works with standard WordPress and WooCommerce forms. Custom forms using different field names may not be supported.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

Names that were already capitalized will remain capitalized. New entries will be saved as users enter them. No data is lost. Your custom particles settings will be preserved if you reactivate the plugin.

How do I backup my database?

Before using the bulk tool, create a database backup using your hosting control panel, a backup plugin, or ask your hosting provider for assistance.
